title: Base change of a compactification
statement:
Let $\square$ be a Cartesian square of schemes
[def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y.
\end{array}
$$
Let $c=(X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y)$ be a compactification of $f$ [def-nagata-compactification], with $j$ an open immersion, $p$ proper and $p\circ j=f$, as in the current blueprint definition. In exchange maps using a chosen compactification $c_f$ of $f$, take $c=c_f$.
Put $\overline X'=\overline X\times_Y Y'$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $\bar g:\overline X'\to\overline X$ and $p':\overline X'\to Y'$, and define $j':X'\to\overline X'$ to be the unique morphism with
$$
\bar g\circ j'=j\circ g',\qquad p'\circ j'=f'.
$$
This is the base-changed factorization of [def-nagata-compactification-base-change]. The maps $g'$ and $j'$ identify $X'$ canonically with $X\times_{\overline X}\overline X'$: the outer rectangle formed by $\square$ (with $f'=p'\circ j'$ and $f=p\circ j$) and the lower square $\square_p$ below are Cartesian, so the upper square with sides $g',j',j,\bar g$ is Cartesian [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting]. The morphism $j'$ is an open immersion [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], $p'$ is proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], and $p'\circ j'=f'$; thus the base change of $c$ along $g$ is the compactification $c'=(j',p')$ of $f'$ [lemma-nagata-compactification-base-change]. Write $\square_p$ for the Cartesian square
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
\overline X'&\xrightarrow{\bar g}&\overline X\\
p'\downarrow&&\downarrow p\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y.
\end{array}
$$
